adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 25.1. Halloween (event week) has a noise-adjusted effect of x1.0, so no uplift. A 4.1% price increase reduces demand; past price hikes show 10-15% sales drop, but this is a small increase. A competitor opening across the street suggests demand loss. Past similar events (e.g., new store nearby) reduced sales by ~15-20% in noisy data. Evidence is limited (one past occurrence), so shrink toward 1.0. No promotion or seasonal ramp. Final multiplier shrunk to 0.92. Downside spread widened slightly due to uncertainty. Confidence: low.

  median 25.1 | 5%-95%: 0.6 - 58.3 | 10%-90%: 5.7 - 41.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
